chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Three Big Forces, Dalio's Foundational Framework

lessons.title: The Short-Term Debt Cycle Recapped: The 5-8 Year Business Cycle Rhythm

body.text: The short-term debt cycle is the only one of Dalio's three forces most people ever consciously track, because it repeats every 5 to 8 years and is driven almost entirely by one visible lever: the RBI's repo rate. This lesson breaks it into five phases and maps them onto a real recent RBI cycle, so that Chapter 2 can build the long-term debt cycle directly on top of it.

children.text: Lesson 1 defined the short-term debt cycle at a high level: the RBI eases, credit and spending accelerate ahead of income, inflation builds, the RBI tightens, growth slows, and the cycle bottoms before the next easing begins. This lesson slows that loop down into five distinct phases and attaches a real, recent RBI cycle to each one, so the pattern is not just theoretical. It closes Chapter 1 and sets up the shift this course makes in Chapter 2, from a single short-term cycle to what happens when eight or ten of these cycles stack on top of each other over decades.
The Five Phases of a Short-Term Debt Cycle

body.caption: The five phases, what the RBI does, and what to watch
headers: What Credit and Growth Data Show

cells: 1. Early Expansion
Rates held low or freshly cut, often after a downturn
Credit growth accelerates off a depressed base; PMI turns above 50
Equities re-rate first, ahead of visible earnings improvement
2. Mid-Cycle Expansion
Rates steady; the RBI is comfortable with the growth and inflation mix
Credit growth and income growth rise together; broad-based earnings growth
Steady equity gains; corporate bond spreads stay tight
3. Late-Cycle Overheating
The RBI begins hiking as inflation runs above its comfort band
Credit growth stays strong but inflation and asset valuations run ahead of fundamentals
Volatility rises; bond yields climb faster than equity earnings can justify
4. Tightening-Induced Slowdown
Rates held high or still rising
Credit growth decelerates sharply; PMI new orders roll over first
Equities de-rate; credit spreads widen from cycle lows
5. Recession or Trough
The RBI pauses, then starts cutting again
Credit growth bottoms out or turns negative; growth data confirms weakness with a lag
Markets typically bottom before the growth data does, anticipating the next easing cycle

children.text: Mapping the Five Phases to a Real RBI Cycle

The clearest recent example of a full short-term debt cycle running through all five phases is the RBI's repo rate path from the pandemic low through the 2022-23 hiking cycle and into the 2025 easing cycle. Phase 1 and 2 ran through the pandemic-era cuts and the recovery that followed. Phase 3 began in May 2022 when the RBI moved to an unscheduled hike as inflation broke above its tolerance band. Phase 4 ran through the fastest hiking cycle in over a decade. Phase 5 arrived once the RBI judged inflation sufficiently under control to begin cutting again in 2025.

body.title: RBI Repo Rate Path, April 2020 to June 2025

body.text: The repo rate figures above are compiled from public RBI Monetary Policy Committee resolutions up to June 2025 and are provided for teaching the shape of a cycle, not as a live data feed. The RBI's MPC meets roughly every two months, so several more decisions will have occurred by the time you are reading this. Always check the RBI's own website for the current repo rate before using it professionally.

stats.label: Pandemic-Era Low
stats.context: Held from April 2020 into 2022, the lowest repo rate in the RBI's modern history

stats.label: Cycle Peak
stats.context: Reached in February 2023 and held for almost exactly two years

stats.label: Total Hike, May 2022 to Feb 2023
stats.context: 250 basis points in under 10 months, among the fastest RBI hiking cycles on record

stats.label: Time From Peak to First Cut
stats.context: The RBI held at the cycle peak before beginning to ease again in February 2025

children.text: Reading the Turn: Signals at Each Phase Boundary

markDefs.definition: The difference between the yield on a longer-dated government bond and a shorter-dated one, or between a bond yield and the prevailing policy rate. A shrinking or negative spread often signals the market expects the central bank to cut rates.

children.text: The phase boundaries in the table above rarely announce themselves cleanly. The most useful signals tend to move before the RBI's own decisions do. The 10-year G-Sec yield relative to the repo rate, a form of

, tends to compress ahead of a pause or a cut. Bank non-food credit growth, published in the RBI's own weekly statistical supplement, decelerates before quarterly GDP prints confirm a slowdown. And PMI new orders, not the PMI headline number itself, tend to roll over one to two quarters before the broader late-cycle to slowdown transition becomes obvious in earnings.

body.title: Late-Cycle Warning Signs vs Early-Cycle Confirmation Signs

columns.label: Late-Cycle Warning Signs
points: Inflation prints running persistently above the RBI's tolerance band
Credit growth still strong even as valuations look stretched relative to earnings
PMI new orders decelerating while the headline PMI still looks healthy
Bond yields rising faster than nominal earnings growth

columns.label: Early-Cycle Confirmation Signs
points: Credit growth accelerating from a depressed, multi-quarter low base
PMI moving back above 50 after a period below it
Bond yields falling or stable while equities begin re-rating
The RBI explicitly signalling an easing bias in its policy statement

body.title: Locate the Current Phase Yourself
steps: Check the RBI's website for its most recent MPC resolution and note the current repo rate and its policy stance: accommodative, neutral, or withdrawal of accommodation
Pull the latest bank non-food credit growth figure from the RBI's Weekly Statistical Supplement and compare it to the same figure a year ago
Check the latest S&P Global India Manufacturing and Services PMI new orders sub-index specifically, not just the headline number
Using the five-phase table in this lesson, write down which phase the current data most closely resembles, and what single data point would confirm or disprove that view over the next quarter

body.title: Do the Rate Math
body.prompt: Starting from the cycle peak of 6.50%, if the RBI cuts the repo rate by 25 basis points at each of four consecutive policy meetings, what is the resulting repo rate, in percent?
body.explanation: Four cuts of 25 basis points each equal 100 basis points, or 1.00%, in total. Subtracting that from the 6.50% peak gives 5.50%, matching the actual level the repo rate reached by June 2025 in the cycle mapped in this lesson.

body.title: Check Your Understanding
body.question: Bank non-food credit growth has been decelerating for two consecutive quarters even though headline PMI is still comfortably above 50, and the 10-year G-Sec yield has started falling relative to the repo rate. Which phase does this combination most resemble?
options: Phase 4, Tightening-Induced Slowdown, moving toward Phase 5
body.explanation: Decelerating credit growth and a falling bond yield relative to the repo rate are both signals the market is pricing in a coming slowdown or rate cut ahead of the data fully confirming it, which is characteristic of the later stages of a tightening-induced slowdown moving toward a trough, even while headline PMI has not yet broken down.

body.text: Every short-term debt cycle runs through the same five phases, but no two cycles start from the same place. The 2022-23 hiking cycle began from a repo rate of 4.00%, itself a historic low. The next cycle will begin from wherever the current easing cycle ends. Whether that starting point represents a genuinely lower debt burden across the economy, or simply more debt carried at a lower interest cost, is exactly the question that separates the short-term cycle covered in this lesson from the long-term debt cycle this course turns to next.

This lesson presents a general educational framework for reading short-term debt cycles and is not investment advice or a market forecast. Repo rate history and other figures are presented as compiled approximations for teaching purposes as of mid-2025; verify current rates, PMI prints, and credit growth data from the RBI and S&P Global before relying on them professionally.

points: The short-term debt cycle moves through five phases: early expansion, mid-cycle expansion, late-cycle overheating, a tightening-induced slowdown, and a recession or trough, before the RBI eases again

The 2020 to 2025 RBI cycle is a clean recent example: a pandemic-era low of 4.00%, a rapid hiking cycle to a 6.50% peak by February 2023, a roughly two-year hold, and an easing cycle beginning in February 2025
Bond yield spreads, bank credit growth, and PMI new orders sub-indices tend to move ahead of the RBI's own decisions and ahead of headline GDP data
Chapter 1 has now built all three of Dalio's forces: productivity growth, the short-term debt cycle mechanics, and why credit itself is the mechanism connecting the two
Chapter 2 moves from a single short-term cycle to what happens across eight to ten of them stacked over decades, which is where the long-term debt cycle actually gets built
